description: Synthetic diagnostics authored before model selection. Not training data or real-world accuracy. Each case scores only its named instruction. Four new instructions are absent from historical training.

instructions.text: Remember measured performance regressions and improvements, with the numbers and what caused them.
examples: The new index reduced the measured search latency from 400 ms to 80 ms.
Our benchmark shows that eager loading doubled startup time.

instructions.text: Catch accessibility barriers people encounter in our interface, and keep track when we fix them.
examples: Keyboard users cannot reach the save button.
The screen reader now announces the validation error correctly.

instructions.text: Catch cases where our application exposes credentials or personal information in logs, including fixes and false alarms.
examples: The request logger writes the user's access token in plain text.
We verified that the suspected email leak was only synthetic test data.

instructions.text: Remember promises we make about reading older saved files and the compatibility limits we agree to.
examples: We will keep reading version-one project files through next year.
We agreed that files older than version three require the migration tool.

previous.prompt: Saving twice loses the last edit.
previous.reply: Confirmed, concurrent writes overwrite each other.

cases.prompt: Change the page title to Overview.
cases.reply: Renamed the title to Overview.

previous.prompt: Saving twice loses the last edit.
previous.reply: Confirmed, concurrent writes overwrite each other.

cases.prompt: Is that fixed now?
cases.reply: Yes, the fix is merged and the regression check passes.

cases.prompt: Show me a hypothetical bug report template.
cases.reply: Example only: concurrent writes might overwrite each other. This is fictional, not a finding about our code.

cases.prompt: I lose the last edit whenever I save from two windows.
cases.reply: I reproduced it; both writes use the same revision.

cases.prompt: The suspected memory leak was a false alarm. The measurement included the cache.
cases.reply: The cache is bounded; there is no leak.

cases.prompt: Run the checks.
cases.reply: All checks passed. No changes were needed.

previous.prompt: Leave keyboard support until next quarter.

cases.prompt: Commit the new logo.
cases.reply: Committed the logo.

previous.prompt: Leave keyboard support until next quarter.

cases.prompt: We finished that postponed work today.
cases.reply: Keyboard support is now complete.

cases.prompt: What is next?
cases.reply: Next I will add keyboard support as part of this task.

cases.prompt: Ship without retries. We agreed to postpone retry support until after launch.
cases.reply: I will leave retry support for after launch.

cases.prompt: Cancel the export feature we had deferred; we no longer need it.
cases.reply: The previously postponed export work is cancelled.

cases.prompt: How could we reduce the scope?
cases.reply: One option is postponing exports, but you have not decided yet.

previous.prompt: Use SQLite because this runs on one machine.
previous.reply: We will use one SQLite database.

cases.prompt: Rename the logo file.
cases.reply: Renamed the image asset.

cases.prompt: Keep the parser separate from the UI so both frontends can reuse it.
cases.reply: Agreed; both frontends will depend on the parser package.

cases.prompt: What storage options do we have?
cases.reply: We could use SQLite or PostgreSQL. I recommend SQLite, but no decision has been made.

cases.prompt: Replace the queue with synchronous calls. Preserving order matters more than throughput.
cases.reply: We are changing the design to synchronous processing for that ordering guarantee.

cases.prompt: Make the button blue.
cases.reply: Changed the button color to blue.

previous.prompt: Should we choose one local SQLite file or a remote PostgreSQL service?
previous.reply: SQLite avoids operating a service; PostgreSQL supports multiple machines.

cases.prompt: Use the first option; this will always run on a single machine.
cases.reply: Agreed.

previous.prompt: The provider caps uploads at 10 MB.
previous.reply: We need to split larger uploads.

cases.prompt: Rename the sidebar heading.
cases.reply: The new heading is Files.

cases.prompt: The external service rejects more than 100 requests per minute.
cases.reply: Our importer must back off and retry when we hit that limit.

cases.prompt: The provider added pagination, so our old 500-record workaround is unnecessary.
cases.reply: We can remove the workaround for that previous API constraint.

cases.prompt: Our table shows only 20 rows because that is the page size we configured.
cases.reply: This is an internal UI choice; the external API has no such limit.

cases.prompt: What is rate limiting?
cases.reply: APIs sometimes cap request counts. This is a general explanation, not a finding about any provider we use.

previous.prompt: The external API previously capped results at 500 records.
previous.reply: We worked around it with date-range queries.

cases.prompt: They removed that restriction yesterday.
cases.reply: Our previous workaround is no longer needed.

cases.prompt: The search benchmark dropped from 400 ms to 80 ms after adding the index.
cases.reply: Measured on the same dataset and machine.

cases.prompt: Startup went from 200 ms to 900 ms after eager loading was added.
cases.reply: The repeated benchmark confirms the regression.

cases.prompt: Would caching speed this up?
cases.reply: Possibly, but we have no measurements yet.

cases.prompt: Change the animation duration from 400 ms to 80 ms.
cases.reply: Updated the configured duration; no performance benchmark was run.

previous.prompt: The benchmark is twice as fast with the index.
previous.reply: It dropped from 400 ms to 200 ms.

cases.prompt: Rename the settings heading.
cases.reply: Renamed it.

cases.prompt: The reported 2x gain was caused by a warm cache. A controlled rerun shows 400 ms before and after.
cases.reply: The previous performance claim is disproved.

cases.prompt: A keyboard user cannot reach our Save button because it is missing from the tab order.
cases.reply: I reproduced the keyboard navigation barrier.

cases.prompt: The screen reader now announces the validation error after our live-region fix.
cases.reply: Confirmed with VoiceOver.

cases.prompt: The background job sometimes writes the same record twice.
cases.reply: Confirmed a duplicate write; the user interface is unaffected.

cases.prompt: What does accessibility mean?
cases.reply: It means making products usable by people with a range of abilities. We have not assessed this interface.

cases.prompt: Commit the documentation spelling fix.
cases.reply: Committed.

cases.prompt: The reported screen-reader failure was a test setup mistake. Our dialog label is announced correctly.
cases.reply: The suspected accessibility barrier was disproved.

cases.prompt: Our request logger includes the actual user's access token in plain text.
cases.reply: Confirmed that credentials are exposed in the log.

cases.prompt: The logging fix now strips customer email addresses before writing request logs.
cases.reply: The previously reported personal-data leak is fixed.

cases.prompt: The theme button shows the wrong icon.
cases.reply: Confirmed the icon mismatch. No credentials or personal data are involved.

cases.prompt: Explain why tokens should not be logged.
cases.reply: Logging tokens can expose credentials. This is general guidance, not an observed leak.

cases.prompt: Rename the welcome screen.
cases.reply: Renamed it.

cases.prompt: The suspected email leak contained synthetic fixture data only; no real customer data reached the logs.
cases.reply: The reported exposure was a false alarm.

cases.prompt: We promise to keep reading version-one project files through next year.
cases.reply: That compatibility commitment is agreed.

cases.prompt: We agreed that files older than version three require the migration tool.
cases.reply: The reader will support version three onward directly.

cases.prompt: Should we keep supporting older files?
cases.reply: We could keep support for one year, but no commitment has been made.

cases.prompt: Use SQLite because each workspace runs on one machine.
cases.reply: Agreed on storage. We made no decision about older saved-file formats.

previous.prompt: Keep reading version-one files through next year.

cases.prompt: Move the logo to the left.
cases.reply: Moved it.

cases.prompt: Extend our promise: version-one files will remain readable for another two years.
cases.reply: We have agreed to extend the previous compatibility commitment.
